title: Anthropic Lets Companies Self-Host Claude Managed Agents
dek: The full agent stack can now run inside a company's own cloud or servers.

facts.label: Self-hosting launches as a private beta
Routing paths for requests to Claude
One supported cloud, with Foundry & Google

caption:
Your AI agents, your servers, your rules. 🔒

Anthropic has opened a private beta that lets companies run Claude Managed Agents entirely inside their own cloud or on-premises setup. Before, only the agent sandbox could live on company hardware. Now the agent server, the session history database, the workers and the credentials can all stay behind a company's own security perimeter.

Teams also choose where requests to Claude go: straight to Anthropic, through Amazon Bedrock, Google's Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry, or through their own gateway. Agent code carries over too, since the core APIs match the hosted version.

The trade-off is real infrastructure work. But for security-focused enterprises that wanted autonomous agents on sensitive code without the data exposure, this removes a big blocker. We're tracking every Claude agent update here at AI Parabellum.

post_caption:
Until now, the only way to keep an entire agent platform in-house was to build one from scratch. Anthropic's new private beta changes that for Claude Managed Agents.

Companies can now run the control plane, session history and credentials themselves, and route Claude requests via Anthropic, a cloud provider or their own gateway. More control, more to manage. ⚙️
